  • Feb 18, 2025 systems

    Legibility is a feature, not a finish

    Most complex software fails at the moment of reading, not the moment of computing. Clarity has to be designed into the system, not sprinkled on at the end.

    6 min →
  • Jan 09, 2025 engineering

    Spend your novelty budget wisely

    Every project has a limited budget for interesting technical choices. Where you spend it — infrastructure or product — quietly decides how the next year feels.

    5 min →
  • Nov 27, 2024 product craft

    Latency budgets are a design tool

    Deciding where your milliseconds go is not just an operations concern. It is one of the earliest and most consequential design decisions you can make.

    7 min →
  • Oct 14, 2024 engineering

    Write migrations you can walk back

    Forward-only is a strategy for systems you fully understand. Most of the time, you do not — so build the road back before you drive down it.

    5 min →

Field notes

Building in public
  • 001 principle

    A system is only as clear as the worst name in it. Renaming is refactoring — treat it with the same seriousness.

  • 002 experiment

    Rebuilt a data table to stream rows instead of paginating. The interesting part was not speed — it was how it changed the way people scanned the data.

  • 003 bookmark

    Revisiting the idea that most caching bugs are actually invalidation bugs wearing a disguise. Keeping a running log of the ones I hit.

  • 004 note

    Latency budgets are a design tool, not just an SRE metric. Deciding early where the 200ms goes shapes the whole interface.

  • 005 principle

    Prefer boring infrastructure and interesting product. The exciting parts of a stack are rarely where the value is.

  • 006 experiment

    Trying to write every migration so it can be reverted without a meeting. Forward-only is a smell more often than a strategy.
